sections.overview: This near-endemic sandgrouse inhabits dry, open country in southern Africa.
sections.identification: The sexes have different plumage; the bird forages on foot.
sections.habitat: From Angola to South Africa, it favors gravel desert, sandy semi-desert and shrubland.
sections.diet: Seeds dominate its diet, with flowers, small fruits and leaves also eaten.
sections.behavior: Males carry water to chicks in belly feathers, whose water-holding structure has been studied.
sections.reproduction: It nests on the ground; both sexes incubate in day and night shifts.
sections.ecology: Compare its arid open habitats with Yellow-throated and Spotted Sandgrouse in their linked profiles.
sections.conservation: The regional account calls it widespread but notes past decline in parts of the Nama Karoo.
